title: Practice Detail (Tabbed Workspace)
description: Practice Detail (Tabbed Workspace) documentation for Provider.
overview: This guide covers practice detail (tabbed workspace) workflows for Provider.

subtasks.title: Practice tab (Primary Contact, Monitoring Details, Program Dates)
subtasks.purpose: Review the practice’s canonical contact record, monitoring configuration and CCM / RPM program windows.

steps.title: Confirm Practice Tab
steps.description: From the Dashboard, ensure the Practice tab is selected (it is the default).

steps.title: Review Primary Contact
steps.description: Review the Primary Contact card: Facility address, Email, Phone 1, Phone 2, Fax and Status (Active / Inactive).

steps.title: Review Program Dates
steps.description: Review the Program Dates table for CCM and RPM — each row shows the program Start date, End date and the number of Days in the current cycle.

steps.title: Scroll to Monitoring Details
steps.description: Scroll to Monitoring Details for the “Do you want eVitals to Monitor your patients” and “Buying Device” answers. Notes This tab is read-only for a Provider — updates to facility, phone or program dates are performed by an Admin / System Admin. Status = Active means the practice is billable in the current cycle; Inactive suppresses new billing events. Program Dates “Days” is the length of the current billing cycle window, not days remaining.

subtasks.title: Admins tab (view practice administrators)
subtasks.purpose: See the practice’s administrator roster and quickly open any admin’s profile for contact details or event history.

steps.title: Open Admins Tab
steps.description: Click the Admins tab in the practice-detail tab bar.

steps.title: Search or Filter Admins
steps.description: Type into Search admins… to filter by name / email, or use the All Status dropdown to filter Active / Inactive.

steps.title: Sort Admins List
steps.description: Click the Status column arrow to sort ascending / descending.

steps.title: Open Admin Profile
steps.description: Click an admin Name (blue link) to open the admin profile, or use the eye icon in the Action column for the same result.

steps.title: Review Admin Audit Log
steps.description: Click Event Logs (bottom-left) to view the practice-level admin audit trail.

steps.title: Change Page Size
steps.description: Change the Show N entries dropdown to change page size; use the pager (top-right) to move between pages. Notes Add / edit / delete of Practice Admins is restricted to Practice Admin, System Admin and Super Admin — the Provider has read-only access. Event Logs opens a chronological list of admin actions (add / edit / status change / login).

subtasks.title: Providers tab (peer roster)
subtasks.purpose: See the practice’s full provider roster (including self) and open any provider profile.

steps.title: Open Providers Tab
steps.description: Click the Providers tab.

steps.title: Search or Filter Providers
steps.description: Use Search providers… to filter by name / email and the All Status dropdown to filter Active / Inactive.

steps.title: Sort Providers List
steps.description: Sort by Status by clicking the header arrow.

steps.title: Open Provider Profile
steps.description: Click a provider Name (blue link) or the eye icon to open the provider profile. Notes The Provider’s own row appears in the grid so they can quickly open their own read-only profile card. Provider add / edit is restricted to Practice Admin and above.

subtasks.title: Caregivers tab (practice caregivers)
subtasks.purpose: See the Practice Caregiver roster with their contact details and open any profile.

steps.title: Open Caregivers Tab
steps.description: Click the Caregivers tab.

steps.title: Filter Caregivers
steps.description: Filter with Search caregivers… and the All Status dropdown.

steps.title: Sort Caregivers List
steps.description: Sort by Status via the header arrow.

steps.title: Open Caregiver Profile
steps.description: Click a Name or the eye icon to open the caregiver profile.

steps.title: Edit Caregiver (If Available)
steps.description: If the pencil icon is visible for the Provider role, click it to edit; otherwise the row is read-only. Notes The blue “+ Add Caregiver” button visible to Practice Admin / System Admin is typically hidden for a Provider — the tab is used for reference. Practice Caregivers are the primary reviewers for the Provider’s patients — the Patient enrolment wizard requires at least one to be assigned.

subtasks.title: Patients tab — RPM view (billing dates, uploads, CPT counters)
subtasks.purpose: Review the RPM patient population for the current billing window with vitals summary, upload activity and CPT-code progression.

steps.title: Open Patients Tab (RPM View)
steps.description: Click the Patients tab. If the RPM toggle (top-right, blue) is not selected, click RPM.

steps.title: Note Billing Window
steps.description: Note the RPM Billing Dates window (e.g., 07-01-2026 – 07-30-2026) shown top-right.

steps.title: Read Summary Cards
steps.description: Read the summary cards: Total Patient (with A / P / L status chips), Recent Uploads (last 24 hours), Missed Uploads (older than 24 hours), Abnormal Readings (needs review) and CPT Billing (99453 / 99445 / 99454 + more counters showing eligible / total).

steps.title: Filter by Cohort Card
steps.description: Click a card’s “click to view all” link to filter the grid to that cohort.

steps.title: Filter Grid Further
steps.description: Use the Search patients by name… box and the All Status dropdown to filter the grid further.

steps.title: Sort by Name
steps.description: Sort the grid by Name using the header arrow.

steps.title: Review Patient Row Chips
steps.description: For each patient row, review chip badges (BP / BG / WT — a chip indicates the patient is monitored for that vital), latest Systolic / Diastolic / Pulse / Glucose / Weight, Last Upload date, # Readings in the current window and Time (accumulated caregiver-review minutes).

steps.title: Open Reading Trend View
steps.description: Red numbers highlight out-of-target readings (e.g., diastolic 111.00 in red) — click the ♥ heart icon next to a value to open the trend / detail view.

steps.title: Add a Patient
steps.description: Click Add Patient (top-right) to enrol a new patient (opens the same wizard covered under Patient Management).

steps.title: Open or Edit Patient
steps.description: Use the eye icon in Action to open the patient dashboard or the pencil icon to edit demographics. Notes

steps.title: CPT Billing shows current cycle eligibility
steps.description: e.g., 99454 requires ≥ 16 upload days in the 30-day window. Status chip A / P / L stands for Active / Paused / Lost-to-follow-up — chip colours match the row Status. The Time column feeds CPT 99457 (first 20 minutes) and 99458 (each additional 20 minutes) — see the CPT Billing card for real-time eligibility.

subtasks.title: Patients tab — CCM view (care-plan status, service time)
subtasks.purpose: Review the CCM patient population for the current CCM cycle with care-plan status, chronic conditions and billing state.

steps.title: Switch to CCM View
steps.description: Click Patients → click the CCM toggle (top-right, next to RPM).

steps.title: Note CCM Billing Window
steps.description: Note the CCM Billing Dates window (e.g., 06-30-2026 – 07-24-2026).

steps.title: Review CCM Summary Cards
steps.description: Review the summary cards: Total Patients (with A / P / L chips), Active Care Plan (provider-approved plans), Complex Care Plan (attested complex CCM), Items Pending Review (care-plan changes awaiting provider sign-off) and CPT Billing (99490 / 99491 / 99439 with eligible / total counters).

steps.title: Jump to Pending Review
steps.description: Click Items Pending Review → click to view all to jump straight to plans awaiting provider approval.

steps.title: Sort & Filter CCM Grid
steps.description: Sort the grid by Patient Name and filter with Search patients by name… and the All Status dropdown.

steps.title: Review Patient Row Details
steps.description: For each row, review DOB, Chronic Conditions, Last Activity, Service Time (accumulated CCM minutes) and Billing state (Pending / Billed).

steps.title: Add or Edit CCM Patient
steps.description: Click Add Patient to enrol a new CCM patient, or use the eye / pencil action icons to open or edit an existing patient.

steps.title: Toggle Back to RPM
steps.description: Toggle back to RPM using the RPM chip at the top-right when finished. Notes Billing = Pending means the CCM claim for the current cycle has not yet been submitted; Billed indicates it has been filed. A CCM patient must have ≥ 2 chronic conditions to be billable under 99490. “Items Pending Review” is the Provider’s CCM inbox — clearing it is required before billing the cycle.

subtasks.title: System Caregivers tab
subtasks.purpose: See the practice’s System Caregiver roster (cross-practice reviewers such as the eVitals monitoring team) and open any profile.

steps.title: Open System Caregivers Tab
steps.description: Click the System Caregivers tab.

steps.title: Filter Caregivers
steps.description: Filter with Search caregivers… and the All Status dropdown.

steps.title: Sort by Status
steps.description: Sort by Status using the header arrow.

steps.title: Open Caregiver Profile
steps.description: Click a Name or the eye icon to open the caregiver profile.

steps.title: Review Assignment Audit Log
steps.description: Click Event Logs (bottom-left) for the audit trail of System Caregiver assignments. Notes System Caregivers are assigned by Super Admin / System Admin and are shared across practices — a Provider can view but not add / edit. The empty state “No system caregivers found” means no System Caregiver is currently mapped to this practice.

subtasks.title: RPM tab (RPM-scoped practice contact)
subtasks.purpose: View the RPM-scoped copy of the Primary Contact / Program Dates / Monitoring Details, used when RPM billing correspondence must reference a different address / phone than the general practice record.

steps.title: Open RPM Tab
steps.description: Click the RPM tab.

steps.title: Review Practice Contact Info
steps.description: Review Facility, Email, Phone 1, Phone 2, Fax, Status and Program Dates (CCM & RPM rows shown for reference).

steps.title: Scroll to Monitoring Details
steps.description: Scroll to Monitoring Details for the RPM monitoring / device answers. Notes When the RPM record matches the general practice contact, this tab mirrors the Practice tab exactly. Read-only for a Provider — updates are performed by Practice Admin / System Admin.

subtasks.title: Configure Schedule & Targets — Daily Schedule
subtasks.purpose: Confirm the practice-wide daily schedule anchors (Wake-up, Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner, Bed) that drive the vital-sign target windows.

steps.title: Open Schedule & Targets
steps.description: Click the Schedule & Targets tab.

steps.title: Review Daily Schedule Times
steps.description: In the Daily Schedule panel, review or update Wake-up Time (required, default 06:00 AM), Breakfast Time (required, 08:00 AM), Lunch Time (required, 12:00 PM), Dinner Time (required, 06:00 PM) and Bed Time (required, 10:00 PM) using the time pickers.

steps.title: Save, Cancel, or Audit
steps.description: Click Save to persist, Cancel to discard, or Event Logs to see who last changed the schedule and when. Notes The five anchors are used as the default cut-offs for the Blood Pressure and Blood Glucose target windows (see 8.2.10 / 8.2.11). Editing this panel updates the whole practice — not just the Provider’s patients. If Save / Cancel are greyed out, the Provider role does not have edit permission on this practice; contact a Practice Admin.

subtasks.title: Configure Schedule & Targets — Blood Pressure Targets
subtasks.purpose: Confirm five time-of-day BP windows (Wake-up / Morning / Noon / Afternoon / Evening) and the Systolic / Diastolic target range for each window.

steps.title: Scroll to BP Targets
steps.description: Scroll to the Blood Pressure Targets panel.

steps.title: Set BP Time Windows
steps.description: For each window (Wake-up, Morning, Noon, Afternoon, Evening — all required), set the Start and End times.

steps.title: Set Systolic/Diastolic Bounds
steps.description: For each Target Range panel below the times, set Systolic Pressure lower / upper bounds and Diastolic Pressure lower / upper bounds (defaults 100/142 systolic wake, 100/130 morning etc., and 50/113 diastolic wake, 50/80 morning etc.).

steps.title: Save BP Targets
steps.description: Click Save (top-right of the panel). Notes The five windows must not overlap — the UI blocks Save if a window Start ≥ End or if two windows overlap. Any BP reading falling outside its window’s target range appears in red on the Patients grid and contributes to the Abnormal Readings summary card. Diastolic values above the upper bound (e.g., 111.00 vs upper 113) are typically flagged red on the grid.

subtasks.title: Configure Schedule & Targets — Blood Glucose Targets
subtasks.purpose: Confirm the eight glucose time windows and their target ranges for the practice.

steps.title: Scroll to Glucose Targets
steps.description: Scroll to the Blood Glucose Targets panel.

steps.title: Review Headline Ranges
steps.description: Review / edit the three headline ranges: Wake-up Target Range (default 60–110), Before-Meal Target Range (60–110), After-Meal Target Range (70–140).

steps.title: Review Bedtime & Midnight Ranges
steps.description: Review / edit Bedtime Target Range (60–110) and Midnight Target Range (60–110).

steps.title: Set Wake-Up Time
steps.description: Set the Wake-up Time (required, default 06:00 AM – 11:00 AM).

steps.title: Confirm Meal Time Windows
steps.description: For each of Before-Breakfast (07:01 AM – 01:00 PM), After-Breakfast (09:01 AM – 03:00 PM), Before-Lunch (11:01 AM – 05:00 PM), After-Lunch (01:01 PM – 09:00 PM), Before-Dinner (05:01 PM – 11:00 PM), After-Dinner (07:01 PM – 12:29 AM), Bedtime (08:30 PM – 02:00 AM) and Midnight (10:00 PM – 10:00 AM), confirm the Start / End times.

steps.title: Save or Cancel Targets
steps.description: Click Save to persist or Cancel to discard. Notes After-Meal target range is intentionally wider (70–140) to accommodate postprandial spikes.

steps.title: Windows that wrap past midnight (e.g., After-Dinner 07
steps.description: 01 PM – 12:29 AM) are supported. Readings outside the window range are highlighted on the Patients grid and inside the patient trend chart.

subtasks.title: Configure Schedule & Targets — Weight Targets
subtasks.purpose: Set the weight, body-fat and BMI target ranges and the Morning / Afternoon / Evening weigh-in windows that drive the Weight (WT) chip badges on the Patients grid.

steps.title: Scroll to Weight Targets
steps.description: Scroll to the Weight Targets panel at the bottom of the Schedule & Targets tab.

steps.title: Review Reference Ranges
steps.description: Review the Recommended Weight Range (-- lb) and Recommended Body Fat Range (-- %) reference labels (auto-populated from the practice defaults).

steps.title: Enter Weight Target Range
steps.description: Enter the Weight Target Range — lower bound (e.g., 66) and upper bound (e.g., 220) in lb.

steps.title: Enter Body Fat Range
steps.description: Enter the Body Fat Target Range — lower bound (e.g., 14) and upper bound (e.g., 27) in %.

steps.title: Set BMI Thresholds
steps.description: In the BMI Target Range row, keep the Underweight column as the BMI label anchor and enter the thresholds for Normal (e.g., 18.5), Overweight (e.g., 25) and Obese (e.g., 30).

steps.title: Set Morning Weigh-In Window
steps.description: Set the Morning weigh-in window — start (e.g., 06:00 AM) and end (e.g., 03:59 PM).

steps.title: Set Afternoon Window
steps.description: Set the Afternoon window — start (e.g., 12:00 PM) and end (e.g., 09:59 PM).

steps.title: Set Evening Window
steps.description: Set the Evening window — start (e.g., 06:00 PM) and end (e.g., 09:59 AM next day).

steps.title: Save Weight Targets
steps.description: Click Save to persist the Weight Targets panel, or Cancel to discard changes.

steps.title: Review Weight Config History
steps.description: Click Event Logs to review historical edits to the weight configuration. Notes Weight and Body Fat values outside the target ranges surface red on the Patients grid and count toward the Abnormal Readings summary card. The BMI thresholds are inclusive lower bounds — a BMI of exactly 25 falls into Overweight, 30 into Obese. The three weigh-in windows overlap intentionally so late-morning or late-evening readings are still tagged; each reading is bucketed by its timestamp. Weight is shown in the practice’s configured unit — check Settings if the unit needs to change from lb to kg.

subtasks.title: Import Patients (bulk upload)
subtasks.purpose: Bulk-enrol patients from a CSV or Excel spreadsheet and assign them to a Provider and Caregiver in one step, instead of running the Add New Patient wizard per patient.

steps.title: Open Import Patients Tab
steps.description: Click the Import Patients tab (rightmost tab in the practice-detail tab bar).

steps.title: Select Owning Provider
steps.description: In the Add Bulk Patients card, open the Provider * dropdown and pick the owning Provider for the imported patients.

steps.title: Select Monitoring Caregiver
steps.description: Open the Caregiver * dropdown and pick the Practice Caregiver who will monitor the imported patients.

steps.title: Upload Patient Spreadsheet
steps.description: Under CSV / Excel File, click Upload CSV/Excel and choose the prepared spreadsheet — the chosen file name replaces “No file chosen”.

steps.title: Submit or Cancel Import
steps.description: Click Import Patients (bottom-right, blue) to submit, or Cancel to abandon the upload.

steps.title: Review Import Results
steps.description: Review the result summary — rows imported, rows failed and a downloadable error report for the failed rows.

steps.title: Correct & Re-Upload Rows
steps.description: Correct the failed rows in the spreadsheet and re-upload only those rows. Notes Provider and Caregiver are both required — the Import Patients button stays disabled until a file is selected and both dropdowns have a value. Duplicate detection uses First Name + Last Name + DOB — matching rows are skipped, not overwritten. Header row must match the template exactly; extra columns are ignored, missing required columns reject the whole file. For RPM patients, Meter Serial Number must be exactly 16 characters or the row is rejected. Task 8.3 — Patient Management
